catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries a waveform-generator byte pattern. cap.device.configure.v1 is the write class, but its binding is the resource-state patch of writable fields and cannot express a 62-byte maximum length with a per-element bound; this action sends the waveform through the upstream set_generator_waveform and reports the length and a checksum of the bytes sent.
catalogue_requests.summary: Send a generator waveform (at most 62 bytes, each at most 0b1111_1111).

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class starts a keep-alive pause on a USB instrument. cap.motion.stop.v1 and cap.motion.estop.v1 are motion stops, not a keep-alive start; this extension starts the upstream pause thread and reports the paused state.
catalogue_requests.summary: Start the upstream keep-alive pause thread.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class stops a keep-alive pause thread on an instrument; cap.motion.stop.v1 is a motion stop. This extension calls the upstream cancel_pause and reports the paused state.
catalogue_requests.summary: Stop the upstream keep-alive pause thread.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue stop class fits a waveform generator: cap.motion.stop.v1 is a motion stop and names motion resource kinds. This extension switches the generator outputs off, stops the keep-alive pause thread, and is the safe-state action for this R1 hardware driver.
catalogue_requests.summary: Switch the generator off and stop the keep-alive pause thread (the safe state).

notes:
Passed on the fake backend with python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/vadter__hantek1008c --backend fake (exit 0, all gates G1 to G9, no findings or warnings; check-report.json). Evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wP-041) and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested this package and no hardware run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the package is a direct Driver over pyhantek1008C:Hantek1008 (the card's decision), not the PythonObjectDriver family helper named in the card's helper field, because the R1 hardware contract needs the decorated @estop and safe-state action. The entry symbols were confirmed in the clone: Hantek1008 at pyhantek1008C.py:782 and Hantek1008CRaw at pyhantek1008C.py:39.

Covered: resource-state reads for active_channels (zero-based ids 0 to 7), time (the real 500-point time axis in seconds), vscales (one vertical scale factor per channel), generator_waveform_max_length (1440), paused, and the last commanded generator_on and generator_speed; cap.device.configure.v1 writes for generator_on and generator_speed, with generator_speed limited to 1 to 750000 rpm by the upstream assertion at pyhantek1008C.py:641; the extensions set_generator_waveform (at most 62 bytes, each at most 0b1111_1111), pause, resume and generator_off; the e-stop and the safe-state action both stop the keep-alive thread and call set_generator_on(False).

The generator_on and generator_speed reads report the last value this driver commanded, because the upstream class has no getter for either (pyhantek1008C.py:632-636); after construction the upstream init1 leaves the generator off at 300000 rpm (pyhantek1008C.py:332-333). The fake starts from those values and returns 500 time points, the same 500-point size as the real time axis; its other starting values and waveform bytes are placeholder test data, never Facts, Limits or references.

NOT COVERED: the sample arrays of request_samples_burst_mode and request_samples_roll_mode. The clone returns per-channel sample lists (or a time axis plus samples); no catalogue class carries a trace array, so this package serves the settings and status scalars and does not transfer samples. Also not bound: get_vscale(channel_id), get_zero_offset(channel_id) and get_zero_offsets(), because a @read takes no input and the zero-offset table is keyed by float scale factors. The upstream README says the offset problem is not solved (README.md:6).

native.py imports the upstream only on the operator-enabled hardware backend and was never imported or run here; the acceptance gate and the fake use only the package fake. The upstream README lists pyusb, overrides, matplotlib and pyqtgraph as dependencies (README.md:1); nothing was installed. The e-stop is a software stop at R1: it switches the generator outputs off and stops the keep-alive pause thread. No line of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not set and none is claimed. The loader refuses the hardware backend of a model-written package only at R2 and R3, so this R1 package is not protected by that rule; use its hardware backend only with a person at the device.
